title: CharForge: rigged, animated game characters from a few words or one image, on a laptop
subtitle: A living research paper - method, measurements and open problems, revised as the experiments run
acknowledgement: Experiments and this living paper were developed with Claude (Anthropic) working in the repository. Script-backed values are included where artifacts exist; some historical and prose claims remain manually maintained and are being audited.

changes: The aberration audit runs and is validated (E102): 22 of 22 checks on a synthetic character with known-size aberrations pass under both skinnings, penetration to the millimetre; the checks exposed three measuring errors (quads re-split by pose, depth capped at 3 cm, false inside readings at open rims and between layers), now fixed. Blender's BVH overlap is a triangle-triangle test, so intersections are real; depth tells contact from penetration.

The roster measured on every frame of every clip: crushed 2.72%, stretched 1.52%, sheared 2.71% of faces; dual quaternion against linear skinning; frames with a body region more than 2 cm inside another 48.44%.

Joint limits measured on each character's own mesh, and every clip held inside them (E128): frames with deep penetration 48.44% -> 34.28%, surface measures and foot slip unchanged. New related work: contact-aware retargeting.

Time (E106 pilot): the multi-view second 3D pass fitted the reference's front worse on 12 of 12 characters and drifted from the picture where its repainted views invented detail; it is now off by default, saving a median 16 of 41 minutes. The end-to-end comparison is still to run.

Audited legacy citations against primary sources: separated the pinned Mixamo mirror count from Adobe's product page, corrected hand-deformation and skinning citations, distinguished Qwen-Image 2.1's checkpoint/license from earlier papers, and narrowed vendor claims.

Recorded TRELLIS.2 research-only materials, the unresolved H3 fine-tune/base-license conflict, and Mixamo mirror access/redistribution uncertainty; added primary license sources and corrected method, limitations, README, and E115 provenance language.
Reconciled E102 prose with current code safeguards (topology/order assertion, centered pop metric, default no-clobber); no Blender runtime validation or new experiment result was performed.
Added primary-source references for stylized AU controls, segmentation reliability, and footskate perception; explicitly limit transfer claims and thresholds.

Tightened planned metric definitions and acceptance protocols for motion truth, dense aberration sampling, scan/retopo distance, part-label calibration, hand pose, runtime delivery, foot-contact parity, provenance/cache validity, and Studio workflows.

Recorded that the browser footAudit still uses a 1 m/s denominator floor and differs in contact sampling from the corrected Blender v2 path; historical results remain unchanged and E122 remains required.

Added the user-requested fast-classifier investigation as E127 at the end of the queue. Model identity, architecture and license remain unverified; discovery and benchmarking are explicitly gated behind earlier queued work.

Research-gap audit across prompt fidelity, geometry repair, part labels, retopology, UVs, runtime texture sampling, deformation, motion truth, engine delivery, provenance and evaluation; added primary-source references and planned experiments E116-E126.

Reopened E029 after finding its legacy max(speed, 1 m/s) denominator understated sub-1 m/s ratios; preserved historical measurements and specified a corrected rerun. E102's candidate-only BVH and cadence-specific pop measures are documented; code changes remain pending Blender runtime validation.
Clarified that the paper build validates references and structure but does not yet link every manually maintained empirical claim to an artifact; E121 tracks that work.

The lab book became this paper: method, evaluation with every number collected from the measurement files (paper/collect.py), related work with verified references, limitations and a roadmap; the chronological lab notebook kept beside it.
Experiment tracker (research/experiments.json, rendered as research/TRACKER.md and Appendix A).

Multi-angle verification (E009) found an elbow folded through the arm (E007), feet off the floor (E008), a comparison video running 25% fast (E010), and showed the kick's score dip was the scorer (E011).

Characters from a few words (E014-E016); hands that meet a bare forearm (E021) and take the face's colour (E020); a realistic face kept from the generator when the reference cannot be laid on it (E022); face positions read at 0.5 mm (E019).
The polish pass: garments fused to the body (E025), folded UV islands (E027), references in the wrong pose (E028), joins left by the arm cut (E026, open).
Hands follow DWPose (E006); the Studio, a local interface to make characters without the command line.
Moves from generated video: retrieval (E001), the fit (E002, E003), aimed limbs (E004), the refine stage (E005); H3 on 24 GB (E030).
Qwen-Image 2.1 as the reference model (E013); three styles, seven characters, the v3.0.0 site.
One entry point, engine conventions (origin, capsule, LODs), real PBR; locomotion that plants its feet (E029).
A local text-to-rigged-character pipeline with its first measurements; dual quaternion skinning in the viewer (E024).
